comparisons.what: Compare uncorrected, Bonferroni and Benjamini-Hochberg at a nominal 5 percent.

constraints: CPU only; under 60 seconds of runtime; fixed random seeds where the run is random, stated in the paper.
Report every number with its uncertainty (for a deterministic result, its numerical error), and say when a result is only a check of the code.
Cite only sources you have actually found and read; if a reference cannot be confirmed, say so rather than citing it.
A short paper of at most 4 pages.
One Python script using numpy (and scipy where it helps), with matplotlib (Agg backend).
Two or three figures that answer the question directly, each with the reference or theory value drawn.
Simulate m tests using one-sided z-tests in which each real effect shifts the test statistic by 2.5.
Evaluate tests at a nominal 5 percent.
